### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/scenarios`, touching **32** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`, `packages/qa/scenarios/src/export/index.ts`, `packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/driver.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/frontend/cli.mdx`  _(via index.json (literal, a string literal in exporterPath; a string literal in galleryRefresh; a string literal in readGalleryVersions))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`, `packages/qa/scenarios/src/export/index.ts`, `packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/driver.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **19** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0f254f474588916ccd3d61450a35adb531d0416f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6ee3ea26cc35eca99d84b78423c81dae4304df4c` — the merge of head `de7c89c59fdbf78cd6421ea0e33309997baa5a40` into base `0f254f474588916ccd3d61450a35adb531d0416f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6ee3ea26cc35eca99d84b78423c81dae4304df4c && git checkout 6ee3ea26cc35eca99d84b78423c81dae4304df4c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0f254f474588916ccd3d61450a35adb531d0416f de7c89c59fdbf78cd6421ea0e33309997baa5a40 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0f254f474588916ccd3d61450a35adb531d0416f && git merge --no-ff de7c89c59fdbf78cd6421ea0e33309997baa5a40

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0f254f474588916ccd3d61450a35adb531d0416f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0f254f474588916ccd3d61450a35adb531d0416f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `de7c89c59fdbf78cd6421ea0e33309997baa5a40`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/31121-scenarios-gallery-refresh.md, packages/qa/scenarios/README.md, packages/qa/scenarios/package.json, packages/qa/scenarios/src/export/cli.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/export/index.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/export/refresh-cli.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/export/refresh.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/driver.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/test/export/refresh.test.ts + packages/qa/scenarios/src/export/exporter.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/export/manifest.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/export/generic.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/export/screenshots.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/export/source.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/cli.ts, packages/qa/scenarios/tsup.config.ts, packages/create-objectstack/src/pkg-utils.ts, .changeset/config.json

Face: declaration. `record-recognisers --template --paths` on the nine files says the paths decide no face and the committed changeset's `Clause-②:` line decides; `readClause2Line` (`clause2-line.mjs`) reads that line as `declared`, value `yes`, no arm, so the review is owed by the `Clause-②: yes` line alone and stands at `TIER_DEFAULT`. `@objectstack/scenarios` is published (PR #31221); its `./export` entry (`src/export/index.ts`, tsup entry `export`) now re-exports `refresh.ts`. Read against `main`: base `7c523aa1`; `origin/main` is three commits past it (`0f254f47`, `007fdb1a`, `7fe019f4`), none under `packages/qa/scenarios`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Entry point, as the order rules it (refresh-cli.ts, package.json) — right.** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/scenarios gallery-refresh --gallery DIR [--cards DIR] [--model M] [--debut] [--work DIR] [--chromium PATH]`, one package script over `tsx src/export/refresh-cli.ts`. It is not a `bin` and not an `exports` key; `files` stays `dist`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, so `refresh-cli.ts` is not packed and the command runs from a checkout only, which is where D2's scheduled task runs it. `--gallery` required, `--model` refuses an empty or flag-shaped value exactly as `run-scenarios --model` does (PR #31204), an unknown flag is refused (`--push` is the pinned example). The library half (`galleryRefresh`) is exported through `./export`, the CLI half is not.
- **The version check (refresh.ts steps 2–3) — right, and the equality it relies on holds by construction.** npm's `latest` dist-tag of `@objectstack/cli` is read through `npm view` behind an injectable `latestVersion` (the only network call in the module); a value that is not `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` is refused before anything runs. The skip reads the per-app `framework.version` of every listed app (the `GalleryIndexSchema` is `strictObject` and carries no top-level version), and fires only when the index lists at least one app and every app states `latest`. The per-app value is the raw `@objectstack/spec` dependency string of the scaffolded project (`projectFrameworkVersion`, `source.ts`), which `create-objectstack` rewrites to the exact version with no range (`syncObjectStackDeps`, `pkg-utils.ts`), and `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/spec` and `create-objectstack` are all in the one `fixed` group of `.changeset/config.json` (110 packages), so npm's latest cli version IS the spec version the run installs. The post-export refusal "an exported app states another framework version" can therefore fire only on a broken release, which is when it should.
- **Run, export, commit (refresh.ts steps 5–8) — right.** `runnerArgv` emits `--only CARDS --modes scratch --packages published --create-version V --out --work --record [--model] [--cards]`, pinned by parsing it with the runner's own `parseArgs` (`createVersion`, `packages: 'published'`, `modes: ['scratch']`, `iterateRun: true`). The export goes into DIR through `exportGallery` with the same guard and recordings the `export-gallery` CLI uses. Then three refusals before any git write: no app exported (naming the exporter's reasons), a listed app on another version, any changed path outside `apps/` and `index.json`. Then `git switch -c export/V`, `git add --all -- apps index.json`, a `diff --cached --quiet` guard, `git commit` under the checkout's own identity. The commit's parent is the checkout's HEAD when the refresh started, pinned (`HEAD^` equals the base).
- **Never pushes, never talks to GitHub — read, not taken on trust.** Every git invocation in `refresh.ts` is `rev-parse --show-toplevel`, `status --porcelain`, `rev-parse --verify refs/heads/...`, `for-each-ref refs/remotes/*/...`, `switch -c`, `add`, `diff --cached`, `commit`, `rev-parse HEAD`. No `push`, `fetch`, `remote`, `checkout`, `reset` or `clean`; `refresh-cli.ts` adds only `mkdtempSync`, `mkdirSync` and the `rmSync` of its own temp directory on a skip. The only process outside git is `npm view`. The test pins the bare remote's refs byte-identical before and after a commit and a skip.
- **Writes only inside DIR, and never over the caller's work.** The exporter writes under `outDir` = DIR (its own `apps/ID` directories, staged and renamed, and `index.json`); the run writes under `--work` (the caller's directory or a fresh temp dir), which is outside DIR by design and holds records, projects and the recording, never gallery files. A dirty checkout, untracked files included, is refused before the npm read; a local `export/V` branch is refused, never reused or reset; a refusal after the export leaves the tree dirty on the caller's branch, uncommitted, and the README says exactly that. Nothing is checked out over, reset or deleted other than app directories the previous index listed, which is the exporter's rule on `main` (PR #30930), not this PR's.
- **`--debut` — right.** One card, the first eligible id (today `asset_lifecycle`, the first of the six `starter` cards; the three `control` cards are refused by `GALLERY_GUARD`), only into a gallery whose index lists no app; the refusal into a listed gallery is an addition the card does not forbid and is pinned (ablation A2).
- **`driver.ts` — a comment-only hunk.** All eleven changed lines are inside the header comment: "a LOCAL Claude Code session …, never a cloud agent" becomes the D2 reading (a local session on the developer's login, or a scheduled Claude Code task in the project's cloud environment on the maintainer's subscription login; an API-billed model still never). `ClaudeCodeDriver`'s refusal of `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` and the strip from spawned children are untouched.
- **`cli.ts` — no behaviour change.** The live screenshot wiring moves into `liveScreenshots(chromium?)`; `main(argv, deps)` keeps its signature and its `deps.screenshots ?? live` order. The one observable difference is that `playwrightBrowser(...)` is no longer constructed when screenshots are off or a test double is given; `playwrightBrowser` does all its work inside `open()` (the `playwright-core` import and the launch), so constructing it did nothing. `liveScreenshots` is a new export of `cli.ts`, which is on no tsup entry: internal.
- **Tests (refresh.test.ts, 17 cases) — no network, no live model, no browser, as the order rules.** Every `galleryRefresh` / `main` call hands a `latestVersion` stub (`npmLatestVersion` is never reached), `screenshots: false`, and a `run` that drives the real crm card through `runCard` with the fixture's scripted model inside `RecordingDriver` (`fixture.ts`). Git is a real local repository with a bare `origin`. The five ablations named in the PR body each remove one refusal and are the right five (version, debut, skip, stray path, dirty tree).
- **README — the three asks are there.** The `gallery-refresh` section, the runbook's "what it runs / what it needs / what it never does", and the task's prompt verbatim (clone, run detached, push only `export/V`, one PR, one deduplicated `Gallery refresh failed` issue). Runbook step 2 builds `'@objectstack/scenarios^...'` (the dependencies, not the package), which is enough because `gallery-refresh` runs `tsx` over `src/`.

### ② Semver level

`patch` is correct. Ruling A in `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` grades by the protocol line alone: `Metadata-protocol: none` means `patch`, and a `minor` beside `none` is refused (the launch-window guard). `Clause-②: yes` with no arm is the right spelling: the `./export` subpath widens from 69 to 84 names (counted as `export` declarations over the barrel's eight files on `main` and nine on the head; `refresh.ts` contributes exactly the 15 the PR body lists, nine values and six types), nothing is removed, renamed or retyped on `./export`, `.`, `./runner` or `./score*`, `cli.ts`'s `main` keeps its signature, no `bin` is added and `package.json` adds one script. No `(narrowing)` arm and no BREAKING banner is owed; the face stays declaration and the tier `TIER_DEFAULT`. The changeset carries both declaration lines; the em-dash prose after `yes` reads as `declared / yes / no arm` through the fleet's reader. Check Changeset is green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Premise deviation: no top-level `framework.version` in `index.json` — faithful.** The card's "when they are equal → skip" presumes one version; the exporter's strict schema carries it per app, and the dev added no index field (which would change the format #31122's check reads). "Equal" is read as ALL listed apps equal, with at least one listed. That is the right reading for a daily refresh: ANY would freeze a straggler app forever, while ALL is safe because a full run rewrites every passing app at `latest` and removes every failing one (the exporter's `kept` arm exists only for `screenshots: false`, which the refresh never passes in production), so one successful run ends with every listed app at `latest`. Edge cases, each read: an empty or absent index runs (an empty gallery is on no release); a mixed index runs, and after the run every app is at `latest` or removed; a prerelease on npm `latest` is a refusal (exit 1), so the scheduled task comments on the one `Gallery refresh failed` issue each day until the dist-tag is corrected, which is the right surfacing of a release incident rather than a quiet skip.
- **The remote-tracking `export/V` skip is an addition — sound, one wording should-fix.** Without it every daily run while the gallery PR awaits review would spend hours of subscription quota and then fail to push an existing branch. It reads only the clone's remote-tracking refs (`refs/remotes/*/export/V`, one component for the remote name, pinned as `origin/export/18.3.0`), no network. Edge: a gallery PR closed unmerged whose branch survives holds the skip for that version until the branch is deleted; the skip line says "awaits review" and does not name that remedy. Should-fix (wording): have the line say the branch must be deleted to run again.
- **After the debut the gallery skips until the next stable release; the README does not say so.** The PR body's acceptance note states it; the runbook the maintainer reads does not. Should-fix (one sentence in the README's `gallery-refresh` section). The design question itself is in ④.
- **Report status `done` with an open question, where the order asks `needs_decision` for a decision outside the rulings.** The dev implemented the rulings exactly as written (no force flag is named) and raised whether to add scope; `done` is defensible, the question is the seat's, no escalation.
- **Deviations 1 and 2 in the report (no labels, no assignees on `pr_create`).** Not a contract matter; the seat labels at landing, as on #31275.
- **Check-runs on this head at the time of this read:** 33 success, among them `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core`, `Test Core` shards 3–8, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Type Check · workspace`, the PR-body guards and `Check PR Size`; 13 skipped (UI, docs, dogfood shards and the opt-in harnesses, none owed by this diff); `Test Core (1/8)` and `(2/8)` still in progress. Landing waits for those two.
- **Overlap with #31309 (`claude/project-thread-zbvjqe`) on `packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`: no textual conflict.** #31309 rewrites the persona-contract bullet at lines 253–262; this PR inserts a new section after line 266. `git merge-tree --write-tree` of the two heads writes a tree and exits 0. #31309's other files (`test/runner/*.test.ts` and runner sources) are untouched here. Whichever lands second rebases without a hunk to resolve.
- **Live model run not measured** (maintainer pause, cloud#3600): the chain is proved on the fixture's recorded crm run; the first real debut is the scheduled task's first run, by design.
- No security findings, no out-of-scope findings in the report.

### ④ Design judgment

The declaration face owes no ④; this is the lane seat's judgment offered on the points the brief asked for.

- **The chain is deterministic and loud.** Every exit is one of three: a one-line skip (exit 0, nothing run), a commit on a fresh local branch, or a refusal that names its reason and leaves no half-state the next run cannot see (a dirty tree or a local branch, both refused on the next run with the remedy in the message). The order of checks spends nothing before it has to: checkout and index first, then one `npm view`, then the two skips, then the cards, and only then hours of model time. The post-export refusals compare the result to what was asked for (the release, the owned paths) rather than trusting the run.
- **The open question — keep as is (A), along the four axes.**
  - *Real need:* the only scenario B serves is "the maintainer wants the full gallery at the debut's version before the next stable release". Releases in this fixed group are frequent (the whole group moves together on every publish), so the wait is short and measured in days, and the need is one-off by definition.
  - *Long-term soundness:* the skip rule is the contract that makes a daily task safe to run unattended; a flag that disables it turns the task's idempotence into a parameter. The need is already met without any new surface: `run-scenarios` and `export-gallery` have no skip and are the two steps `gallery-refresh` composes, so a maintainer who wants the full gallery at V today runs them by hand and commits, exactly as before this PR. The escape hatch exists; a second one adds nothing but a way to misuse the first.
  - *Making AI mistakes structurally harder:* the scheduled task is an AI following a prompt. Today the prompt has no spelling that can run every card twice at one version; with `--force` in the vocabulary, one misread of "the gallery looks stale" spends hours of the maintainer's subscription quota and opens a duplicate PR. The absence of the flag is the guard.
  - *Startup-stage scope:* a new flag defaults to no, the ruling names none, and no maintainer sentence asks for one. The stateless debut (the prompt adds `--debut` whenever the index lists no app) is the right companion: it needs no memory and no second mode.
  So A, with the one README sentence in ③ so the day-after skip is expected rather than puzzling. If the maintainer does want the full gallery before the next release, the answer is the two manual commands, not a flag.
- **The remote-branch skip is the right kind of addition.** It is a cheaper, quieter outcome on a state the card did not enumerate (a pushed branch awaiting review), it reads only local refs, and it refuses rather than overwrites when the branch is local. The one gap is the wording named in ③.
- **Nothing speculative.** `--work` and `--chromium` mirror the existing CLIs; `--cards DIR` keeps the meaning it has in both sibling commands rather than acquiring a second one (card ids), which the PR body rightly calls a trap; scratch mode only is what the exporter's pass rule already owes. The library exports are the pieces a caller would need to drive the same chain from code (the plan, the body, the skip reading), none is a hook for another mode.

## 席位核对

**Verdict: ACCEPT** · head `de7c89c59fdbf78cd6421ea0e33309997baa5a40` · card #31121 · report 6715227221 · contract review 6715336052 (PASS, declaration face, TIER_DEFAULT).

- **Shape:** draft → `main`, 9 files, +911/-10, all inside `packages/qa/scenarios/**` plus one changeset. NOT governed. `main` is 3 commits past the base, and none touch `packages/qa/scenarios`. #31309 shares only the package README, on different hunks, and `git merge-tree` shows no conflict.
- **Order, read in the diff:** this is the repo half only. The entry is `gallery-refresh --gallery DIR [--cards …] [--model ALIAS] [--debut]`. It reads the npm latest-stable version through an injectable reader, stubbed in every test.
  - **Skip rule:** it skips quietly only when every listed app is at that version.
  - **Otherwise:** it runs, exports and commits on a local `export/<version>` branch.
  - **Never pushes:** the reviewer read every git call, and there is no push, fetch, remote, reset or checkout. A dirty tree and an existing `export/<version>` are both refused.
  - **Debut:** `--debut` exports one card.
  - Also delivered: the `driver.ts` header names D2, and the README carries the runbook.
- **Premise deviation (no top-level `framework.version` in `index.json`, so the skip reads every app's version): faithful.** ALL-equal is the safe reading, because ANY-equal would freeze a straggler. An empty index runs, and a prerelease on `latest` is refused loudly.
- **Open question (`--force` after a debut): seat ruling, keep as is, no flag.** A new flag defaults to no. The escape hatch already exists with no new surface: `run-scenarios` plus `export-gallery` run by hand. The flag's absence keeps an unattended task from spending quota on a misread.
- **Clause-②:** `yes`. `./export` gains 15 names (69 → 84), all from `refresh.ts`. No existing export changes: `cli.ts` extracts a helper and keeps `main`'s signature, and the `driver.ts` hunk is comments only. No `bin`, and `files` is unchanged. `patch` with `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct.
- **Gates:** local, 74/74 derived gates exit 0, and 5 ablations went red and were restored. Automerge waits for the required check-runs on this head.
- **Wording nits, not blocking, for the next PR that touches the README:**
  - Say in the runbook that after `--debut` the gallery skips until the next stable release.
  - Say that a gallery PR closed unmerged with its `export/<version>` branch kept holds the skip until that branch is deleted.
- **Landing:** under 「按照 pm-dispatch 规则复核过的都授权」 (2026-10-25T11:35Z) and 「你应该使用 pm-dispatch 技能审核和落地pr」 (2026-11-07T16:59Z): `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` now.
